name: AL-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+33 district is among the most Republican seats in the country
Aderholt holds a roughly 65-to-1 fundraising edge ($750K on hand vs. $400)
Prediction markets price a Republican win near 99%
No polls or expert ratings track the race
model.rationale: The R+33 district, Aderholt's long incumbency, and a massive financial advantage leave the Democratic nominee with no realistic path; prediction markets price a Republican win at near certainty.
model.watch: Only a major scandal or an unprecedented national wave against Republicans could put this seat in play; any late polling would help refine the expected margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 4th district is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 33 points to the right. Robert Aderholt, the longtime incumbent, is seeking another term and holds a decisive financial advantage: he has raised about $1.02 million and had roughly $750,000 on hand, while Democratic nominee Amanda Pusczek has raised about $15,600 with under $500 available. No public polls or expert ratings track the race, and prediction markets price a Republican win at roughly 99%.

With no competitive threat to the incumbent and no signs of outside spending or late-breaking developments, the race has drawn little attention. The fundamentals — district lean, incumbency, and money — all point the same direction, and the expected margin sits well beyond the range where campaign activity alone could close the gap. The seat is safely in Republican hands barring an extraordinary, unforeseen event.
